statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL states that only major version 18 is affected and that versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116329/. The flaw is in the statistics import functions added in PostgreSQL 18 (pg_restore_relation_stats and pg_restore_attribute_stats, src/backend/statistics/attribute_stats.c), which do not exist on the REL_16_STABLE branch. This owner publishes PostgreSQL 16 only (16.13-r0 through 16.16-r0 for Alpine 3.23), and neither function name appears in the 16.16-r0 server binary or its system catalog bootstrap file.

PostgreSQL states that only major version 18 is affected and that versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116329/. The flaw is in the statistics import functions added in PostgreSQL 18 (pg_restore_relation_stats and pg_restore_attribute_stats, src/backend/statistics/attribute_stats.c), which do not exist on the REL_16_STABLE branch. This owner publishes PostgreSQL 16 only (16.14-r0 through 16.16-r0 for Alpine 3.24), and neither function name appears in the 16.16-r0 server binary.

CVE-2026-116329 (PostgreSQL statistics import type confusion executes arbitrary code) affects only PostgreSQL 18: the PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116329/, says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected and lists 18.7 as the only fixed release. The flaw is in pg_restore_attribute_stats, part of the statistics import functions added in PostgreSQL 18; the fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/d41c9fad0856d73cc0613d322b669bf10e91dd77, changes src/backend/statistics/attribute_stats.c and is marked back-patch through 18. The PostgreSQL 17.12 source (tag REL_17_12) has no attribute_stats.c or relation_stats.c and its catalog defines neither pg_restore_attribute_stats nor pg_restore_relation_stats, and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, do not list this CVE. The postgres server binary and the postgres.bki catalog file in every published DHI postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, contain neither function name, while the same check matches in the postgresql18 18.7 builds. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-116329 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-116329), but upstream's own advisory places PostgreSQL 17 outside the affected range.
